requirements: Reproduce the llvm-autofix agentic harness paper, including the benchmark construction, the minimal agent, and the evaluation of frontier LLMs on LLVM middle-end bug repair.

sub_tasks.requirements: Set up the LLVM source tree, build system, and required external tools (opt, alive2, llvm-lit, FileCheck, gdb, llvm-extract) at specified base commits so that reproducers can be built and executed.
Acquire the LLVM source tree and check out per-issue base commits used by llvm-bench.
Code has been implemented to clone the llvm/llvm-project repository from GitHub into a controlled local path used by the harness.

verification.spec: Import the harness Python module and locate the function/class responsible for repository setup (e.g., llvm_autofix.setup.clone_llvm). Inspect its source to confirm it invokes `git clone https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project` (or an equivalent GitHub URL) into a configurable local path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to check out an arbitrary LLVM commit hash (the per-issue base commit) into a working tree without leaving the tree dirty.

verification.spec: Call the checkout function with two different LLVM commit hashes on a shared working tree and verify HEAD matches each requested SHA and `git status --porcelain` is empty after each checkout (no untracked or modified files leaked between checkouts).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a base commit is not buildable, the harness walks back through the git history of the main branch to pick the most recent buildable commit and adjusts the reproducers and golden patch accordingly.

verification.spec: Construct a test case where the nominal parent-of-fixing-commit is intentionally broken (fails to configure/build). Invoke the base-commit resolution routine and verify it walks back along main to select the most recent buildable ancestor, and that it rebases/adjusts the reproducer paths and golden-patch diff so both still apply cleanly on the chosen commit.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to reset the LLVM working tree to the initial clean state of a given bug (matching the semantics of the reset() tool), discarding any prior agent edits.

verification.spec: After checking out a bug's base commit, apply an arbitrary edit via the harness's edit tool, then invoke reset(). Verify `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` report a clean tree identical to the initial state right after checkout.

sub_tasks.requirements: Configure and build LLVM at a chosen commit with the required options, targets, and diagnostic features.
Code has been implemented to invoke CMake/Ninja to configure the LLVM build with debug information and assertion checks enabled, as required by the Setup & Build tool category.

verification.spec: Invoke the harness build API on a tiny prepared LLVM checkout (or dry-run mode) and capture the emitted cmake/ninja command line. Assert the command includes -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug (or RelWithDebInfo with -g) and -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON, and that ninja is invoked afterwards.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to build LLVM for the x86 target by default and to accept an alternative target triple (e.g. s390x-linux-gnu, aarch64) when specified by the issue's reproducer command line.

verification.spec: Invoke the build wrapper with (a) no target argument and (b) target=s390x-linux-gnu. Verify (a) produces an opt binary whose default target triple contains x86_64 and (b) produces an LLVM build whose `opt -mtriple=s390x-linux-gnu ...` succeeds on a reproducer that requires the SystemZ backend.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to run an incremental rebuild of LLVM after an agent edit so that subsequent test invocations see the modified sources without a full clean build.

verification.spec: Build LLVM once, record the timestamp of a compiled object file for a specific source file (e.g., InstCombine). Apply a small edit to that source via edit(), invoke the rebuild path, and verify (a) the object file's mtime updated, (b) unrelated object files' mtimes did not change, and (c) opt now reflects the edit.

sub_tasks.requirements: The build wrapper surfaces build failures to the caller with the compiler error text, so downstream tools (test, reproduce) can distinguish build failures from test failures.

verification.spec: Inject a deliberate C++ syntax error into an LLVM source file, run the build wrapper, and verify it returns a non-zero status plus a structured error object whose message includes the compiler's error line (file:line: error: ...). Then have a downstream test() call observe a distinct 'build_failed' status rather than 'tests_failed'.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide a controlled OS-level execution environment matching the paper's setup.
The harness runs agent actions inside an ubuntu:24.04 container image and exposes the standard bash tools (grep, sed, find, etc.) that mini-SWE-agent depends on.

verification.spec: Locate the harness Dockerfile or container spec and assert its FROM line references ubuntu:24.04. Additionally confirm the image installs (or preserves) standard bash utilities grep, sed, find, awk (e.g., via apt-get install or being present in base image).

sub_tasks.requirements: The environment enforces per-action isolation so that directory changes and environment-variable assignments do not persist across separate action invocations (matching the mini-SWE-agent subshell semantics).

verification.spec: Send two consecutive actions to the shell environment: action 1 = `cd /tmp && export FOO=bar`; action 2 = `pwd && echo FOO=$FOO`. Verify action 2 reports the harness's default cwd (not /tmp) and FOO= (empty), confirming per-action subshell isolation.
verification.paper_cite: Section E mini-SWE-agent system prompt (Important Rules #3)

sub_tasks.requirements: The harness blocks forbidden commands (rm, curl, wget, git, ssh, apt, etc., per the mini-SWE-agent system prompt) so that agents cannot bypass validation or fetch external data.

verification.spec: Submit each forbidden command (rm, curl, wget, git, ssh, scp, ftp, telnet, ping, traceroute, nslookup, dig, nmap, apt, apt-get, yum, dnf, pacman, brew) as an action and verify the harness rejects/blocks it (non-zero status and an explanatory message) instead of executing it, without terminating the whole run.
verification.paper_cite: Section E mini-SWE-agent system prompt (Important Rules #4)

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the agent-facing tool categories of llvm-autofix (Setup & Build, Reproduce & Cause, Explore & Debug, Edit & Patch, Test & Validate, Benchmark & Evaluate), exposing the specified tool signatures from Appendix B.1.
Provide the Setup & Build tools that configure and build LLVM at a specified commit/target with the requested build options.
Code has been implemented that exposes a Setup & Build tool taking a commit hash (and optional target) and checking out the corresponding LLVM source tree state before building.

verification.spec: Call the Setup & Build tool with (commit=<sha>, target=<optional triple>) and verify (a) the working tree HEAD equals <sha> prior to building, (b) the build succeeds against that source state, and (c) omitting `target` yields an x86 build while passing an alternative triple yields a build whose opt accepts `-mtriple=<triple>`.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports building LLVM for x86 with debug information and assertion checks enabled by default (matching the paper's stated build profile).

verification.spec: Build LLVM via the harness default profile and inspect the generated CMakeCache.txt (or equivalent): verify LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD contains X86, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is Debug or RelWithDebInfo, LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON, and that opt --version reports an assertion-enabled build.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that caches or incrementally rebuilds LLVM after edits so that Test & Validate does not require a full clean build on every invocation.

verification.spec: Time a first invocation of Test & Validate on a fresh checkout (cold build). Then apply a one-line edit to a single .cpp file and re-invoke Test & Validate; verify the second invocation completes in substantially less wall-clock time (e.g., <25% of the cold time) and that ninja/make reports only the touched translation unit(s) as rebuilt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that surfaces build errors (compilation failures, linker errors) as agent-consumable structured feedback rather than raw multi-thousand-line logs.

verification.spec: Inject a compilation error into an LLVM source file, run build via the harness, and verify the returned error object is a compact structured summary (e.g., <200 lines) containing file:line and the error diagnostic, rather than the full raw ninja/clang log; log size returned should be bounded regardless of underlying compiler output length.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide the Explore & Debug tools exposing find, grep, list, read, code, docs, langref, debug, and eval with the exact signatures in Appendix B.1.
The find tool is implemented with signature find(pat: str, dir: str) and recursively lists files matching the pattern under the given directory.

verification.spec: Import the harness tool module and confirm a callable `find(pat, dir)` exists. Create a temporary directory with files a.cpp, b.txt, subdir/c.cpp. Call find(pat='*.cpp', dir=<tempdir>) and assert the returned list contains a.cpp and subdir/c.cpp but not b.txt (recursive search).

sub_tasks.requirements: The grep tool is implemented with signature grep(args: str) that forwards arguments to a grep-like search over LLVM sources and returns matching text with file locations.

verification.spec: Import the harness and call grep(args='-rn "getEntryCost" llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize') on a checked-out LLVM tree. Assert the returned string is non-empty, contains one or more 'file:line' style entries, and that at least one match points to an existing file under llvm/lib/.

sub_tasks.requirements: The list tool is implemented with signature list(dir: str) that returns files and directories under the given directory.

verification.spec: Call list(dir='llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine') on a checked-out LLVM tree. Assert the return value enumerates known files (e.g., 'InstCombineCalls.cpp', 'InstructionCombining.cpp') and includes subdirectories where present. Also verify list on a non-existent directory returns a clear error rather than raising.

sub_tasks.requirements: The read tool is implemented with signature read(file: str, pos: int, k: int) that returns k lines starting at line pos of the given file.

verification.spec: Call read(file='llvm/include/llvm/IR/Instructions.h', pos=100, k=20). Assert the returned content contains exactly 20 lines corresponding to lines 100-119 of the file (cross-check via `sed -n '100,119p'`). Also test pos beyond EOF returns a truncated result gracefully.

sub_tasks.requirements: The code tool is implemented with signature code(func: str) that resolves the LLVM function name (including qualified names such as llvm::VPTransformState::get) and returns its source.

verification.spec: Call code(func='llvm::VPTransformState::get') and code(func='InstCombinerImpl::visitCallInst') on a built LLVM tree. Assert each returns the corresponding function's source body (contains the function signature and matching closing brace), and that qualified names are resolved to the correct file under llvm/lib/ or llvm/include/.

sub_tasks.requirements: The docs tool is implemented with signature docs(func: str) that returns documentation (including inline comments/Doxygen) for the specified LLVM function.

verification.spec: Call docs(func='llvm::VPTransformState::get'). Assert the return includes the Doxygen/comment block immediately preceding the function declaration/definition (e.g., contains '///' or '/**' style comments) and is non-empty. Compare against a manually extracted comment block for the same function.

sub_tasks.requirements: The langref tool is implemented with signature langref(inst: str) that returns the LLVM Language Reference entry for the specified LLVM IR instruction.

verification.spec: Call langref(inst='getelementptr') and langref(inst='icmp'). Assert each returns the LLVM LangRef section for that instruction (contains the instruction keyword, a 'Syntax' or 'Semantics' subsection, and text sourced from LangRef.rst/html).

sub_tasks.requirements: The debug tool is implemented with signature debug(cmd: str) that forwards commands to a persistent gdb session attached to opt running the current reproducer.

verification.spec: After Stage-I Setup pauses opt in gdb, call debug(cmd='bt') via the tool interface. Assert the returned string contains a backtrace (multiple '#0', '#1' frame lines). Then call debug(cmd='frame 0') and assert the response reflects a frame change (subsequent info reports frame 0). Confirm the gdb session is persistent across calls (same PID).

sub_tasks.requirements: The eval tool is implemented with signature eval(expr: str) that evaluates a C++/gdb expression against the current LLVM internal state at the active breakpoint.

verification.spec: With gdb paused at a breakpoint inside an LLVM pass on a prepared reproducer, invoke eval(expr='<some local variable name>') via the harness tool interface. Assert the returned string is gdb's rendered value of that variable (matches manual `gdb -ex 'p <expr>'` output).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports setting agent-specified breakpoints (e.g., before the crashing function or before the first transformation) so debug/eval expose meaningful state.

verification.spec: Run Stage I Setup on (a) a crash issue and (b) a miscompilation issue from llvm-bench. Attach to the launched gdb session and query `info breakpoints`. Assert a breakpoint exists before the crashing function for the crash case, and before the first optimization transformation for the miscompilation case. Also verify `debug(cmd='bt')` at pause shows the process is stopped at the intended location.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that debug and eval maintain the gdb process across successive tool calls (e.g., frame navigation followed by expression evaluation) rather than restarting per call.

verification.spec: After Stage I pauses gdb, call debug(cmd='frame 3') then eval(expr='WidePhi') (or another local variable known to exist in that frame). Assert eval returns a value consistent with being in frame 3 (not frame 0), demonstrating the gdb process persisted between the two tool calls. Additionally verify the gdb PID is unchanged across the two calls.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide the Edit & Patch tools exposing edit, preview, and reset with the specified signatures and semantics.
The edit tool is implemented with signature edit(file: str, text: str, replace: str) that replaces the substring text with replace inside the given LLVM source file.

verification.spec: Create a temporary file with contents 'hello world foo bar'. Call edit(file=<tmp>, text='foo', replace='baz') via the harness tool interface. Read the file back and assert it now contains 'hello world baz bar'. Additionally verify that when text is not present, the tool returns an error rather than silently succeeding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that makes edit fail (with structured feedback) when the search text is ambiguous or not found, so failures surface as ToolLimit-eligible errors rather than silent corruption.
The preview tool is implemented with signature preview() returning the accumulated agent edits as a unified diff against the base commit.

verification.spec: After making one or more edits via the edit tool, call preview(). Assert the return is a valid unified diff (contains '--- '/'+++ ' headers and '@@' hunks) against the base commit, and that applying the diff via `patch -p1` to a fresh base checkout reproduces the current working tree exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reset tool is implemented with signature reset() that restores the LLVM working tree to the bug's initial state (base commit contents), discarding all agent edits.

verification.spec: Initialize an issue via the harness (base commit checked out), perform an edit() to modify an LLVM source file, then call reset(). Assert the file's contents on disk now match the base commit's version exactly (e.g., via git diff --quiet against the base commit).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces an edit-call budget (default 25 edit calls per issue, per Section 3) and reports a ToolLimit failure when exceeded.

verification.spec: Import the agent module and instantiate the llvm-autofix-mini agent (or its edit-tracking component) with the default configuration. Verify that (1) the configured edit-call limit defaults to 25, e.g. by reading the config attribute (assert agent.edit_limit == 25 or equivalent), and (2) simulate/inject 25 successful edit tool calls followed by a 26th call: the 26th call must not be executed as a normal edit and the agent must terminate the run with a failure whose category/label is 'ToolLimit' (case-insensitive substring match acceptable). Also confirm the same limit is applied independently to the online test tool. The test should stub out actual LLVM builds so it runs quickly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide the Test & Validate tools exposing test(), rebuilding LLVM, running reproducers and regression tests, and supporting online/offline validation modes.
Code has been implemented that includes the issue's reproducers themselves in the test set run by test().

verification.spec: For an llvm-bench issue with N reproducer files, invoke test() on the unpatched base commit. Assert the executed test set (captured via lit's --show-tests or trajectory log) contains all N reproducer file paths, and that failures on the unpatched base include the reproducers themselves.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs regression tests from the inferred erroneous middle-end component (e.g., InstCombine) as part of the online test suite.

verification.spec: For an issue whose inferred erroneous component is InstCombine, invoke test() and capture the lit invocation. Assert that llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/ is included in the test paths, and that the number of tests executed is on the order of hundreds (matching the ~722 average component-specific tests reported in Table 1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented supporting extended offline validation that additionally runs regression tests from other middle-end components (e.g., SLPVectorizer) beyond the inferred component.

verification.spec: Run offline validation with the 'extended' flag enabled on an InstCombine issue. Assert the executed test set additionally includes at least one other middle-end component's directory (e.g., llvm/test/Transforms/SLPVectorizer/) beyond the inferred component, verified via the captured lit command line.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that wires llvm-lit / FileCheck / opt / alive2 as the underlying test drivers invoked by test(), without introducing random fuzzers such as csmith.

verification.spec: Inspect the source of the test() implementation. Assert it invokes `opt`, `alive2` (for miscompilation validation), and `llvm-lit`/`FileCheck` (for regression tests), and that no reference to `csmith` or other random program generators appears anywhere in the harness source (grep -r csmith returns empty).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports both online validation (during agent execution, called via test()) and offline validation (after agent execution) as configurable modes.

verification.spec: Run the harness in mode='online' and confirm the agent can call test() during its ReAct loop and receive results. Then run mode='offline' and confirm test() is not exposed to the agent but is invoked post-hoc in Stage IV, producing a validation verdict. Both modes should be selectable via a config flag/CLI argument.
verification.paper_cite: Section 2.1 Test & Validate; Section 2.3 Stage IV

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces an online-test call budget (default 25 test calls per issue) and reports a ToolLimit failure when exceeded.

verification.spec: Run the agent (or invoke the tool layer directly) and call test() 26 times. Assert that the 26th call returns/raises a ToolLimit failure indication and that the harness records the failure category as ToolLimit for online-test overuse. Confirm the default limit constant equals 25.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that returns concise failure feedback from test() (failing test names and diagnostic snippets) rather than raw multi-megabyte lit logs.

verification.spec: Induce a test failure by injecting a broken patch, then call test(). Assert the returned string is bounded (e.g., <= 64K characters), lists failing test names/paths explicitly, includes a short diagnostic snippet per failure, and does NOT contain the full raw lit stdout (verify size < raw log size).

sub_tasks.requirements: Cross-cutting tool infrastructure: a uniform agent-facing interface, budget enforcement, and per-tool behavior verification consistent with Table in Appendix B.1.
Code has been implemented exposing all tools with a single dispatcher/registry that validates the tool name and argument schema against the signatures in Appendix B.1 before execution.

verification.spec: Invoke the tool dispatcher with (a) an unknown tool name, (b) a known tool with a missing required argument, and (c) a known tool with a wrong-type argument. Assert each case returns a clear validation error without executing side effects. Additionally invoke a valid call and assert it dispatches correctly. Confirm the dispatcher enumerates all Appendix B.1 tools (find, grep, list, read, edit, preview, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, test).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit/integration test suite exists that exercises each tool listed in Appendix B.1 (find, grep, list, read, edit, preview, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, test) on at least one canonical llvm-bench issue and asserts expected structured output.

verification.spec: Run the test suite (e.g., `pytest tests/tools/`) against the harness on one canonical llvm-bench issue. Assert every tool in {find, grep, list, read, edit, preview, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, test} has at least one passing test that asserts on structured output. Verify via coverage report that each tool's entrypoint is executed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that isolates each issue's environment (LLVM checkout, build artifacts, gdb session) so that RuinLLVM situations in one issue do not corrupt evaluation of subsequent issues.

verification.spec: Run evaluation on two issues sequentially where the first agent deliberately corrupts the LLVM tree (RuinLLVM: e.g., deletes llvm/lib/IR/Instructions.cpp). Assert the second issue evaluation still starts from a clean LLVM checkout (verify file exists, base commit matches expected SHA) and completes normally, demonstrating per-issue isolation (e.g., separate workdirs or containers).
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.2 (RuinLLVM failure mode); Section 2.1 Benchmark & Evaluate

sub_tasks.requirements: Verify the composition, per-split statistics, affected component distribution, and llvm-bench live subset match Table 1, Figure 2, and Appendix A.2/A.3.
The llvm-bench dataset artifact exists with the expected schema (per-issue fields for type, fixing_commit, base_commit, reproducers, golden_patch, metadata, component labels, and split label).

Code has been implemented that loads the llvm-bench dataset and exposes each issue with fields: type (crash|miscompilation), fixing_commit, base_commit, reproducers (list), golden_patch, metadata (title/description/timestamps/labels), affected component(s), and split (easy|medium|hard).

verification.spec: Import the dataset loader (e.g., `from llvm_bench import load_dataset`), iterate the first record, and assert it has attributes: type, fixing_commit, base_commit, reproducers (list), golden_patch, metadata (with title/description/timestamps/labels), affected_component(s), split. Assert type is one of {'crash','miscompilation'} and split is one of {'easy','medium','hard'}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that assigns each issue to exactly one of the three splits {easy, medium, hard} based on golden-patch scope: easy = single function edited, medium = multiple functions in a single file, hard = edits spanning multiple files.

verification.spec: Iterate over all issues in the produced llvm-bench dataset; for each, re-derive #Files and #Funcs from the golden patch and assert the split label matches the rule: split=='easy' iff funcs<=1 AND files==1; split=='medium' iff funcs>1 AND files==1; split=='hard' iff files>1. Assert every issue has exactly one split label.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that flags every issue as belonging to the llvm-bench live subset if and only if it was collected within the most recent year relative to the construction cutoff (Aug 26, 2024 through Aug 26, 2025).

verification.spec: For each issue in the produced dataset, read its fixing-commit date. Assert the boolean 'live' flag is True iff the date is within [2024-08-26, 2025-08-26], and False otherwise. Also assert the count of issues with live==True equals 229 for the paper snapshot.
verification.paper_cite: Section 2.2 One subset: llvm-bench live; Table 1

sub_tasks.requirements: Full llvm-bench composition statistics (Table 1 upper half) are reproduced.
Code has been implemented that computes and reports the total number of reproducible issues in the full llvm-bench dataset.

verification.spec: Run the dataset-statistics script on the produced llvm-bench full split and read the reported '#Bugs' for the full row. Compare to the paper's value 334.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported total number of reproducible issues in full llvm-bench equals 334.

verification.spec: Load the llvm-bench dataset index file produced by the benchmark construction pipeline and count the total number of entries. Assert count == 334.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported crash / miscompilation counts for full llvm-bench equal 222 crashes and 112 miscompilations.

verification.spec: Group llvm-bench issues by their bug type label ('crash' vs 'miscompilation') and count each. Assert crashes == 222 and miscompilations == 112.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported number of directly-affected middle-end components (#Comp) for full llvm-bench equals 64.

verification.spec: For each of the 334 llvm-bench issues, extract the set of directly-affected middle-end components from the golden patch (files changed under llvm/lib/Transforms/*, llvm/lib/Analysis/*, etc.). Take the union across all issues and assert its cardinality equals 64.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported average number of reproducers per issue (#Rep) for full llvm-bench equals 1.4 (i.e., approximately 1.41).

verification.spec: Compute the mean number of reproducers per issue across the full llvm-bench dataset: sum(len(issue.reproducers) for issue in dataset) / len(dataset). Compare to the paper's reported 1.4 (≈1.41).

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported average number of component-specific regression tests per issue (#Reg) for full llvm-bench equals 722.2.

verification.spec: Compute the mean number of component-specific regression tests per issue across the full llvm-bench dataset: mean(len(issue.component_regression_tests) for issue in dataset). Compare to the paper's reported 722.2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported average golden-patch size for full llvm-bench matches 17.1 edited lines, 1.6 edited functions, and 1.2 edited files (Fixes columns of Table 1).

verification.spec: Compute average edited lines, functions, and files per golden patch across all 334 full-llvm-bench issues; verify values equal 17.1 / 1.6 / 1.2 respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported average reproducer size across all issues equals 49.7 lines of LLVM IR code.

verification.spec: Compute the average line count of all reproducer LLVM IR files across all issues in llvm-bench full and verify it equals 49.7.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reported number of middle-end components indirectly affected by full llvm-bench issues equals 176 (out of 184 total middle-end components under LLVM 21.1.0 -O3).

verification.spec: Using the LLVM 21.1.0 -O3 pipeline component list (184 total), compute the union of components indirectly affected by any of the 334 llvm-bench issues (via call/dependency graph or the harness's indirect-component metadata). Assert the count equals 176.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-split statistics for the full llvm-bench (easy/medium/hard rows of Table 1 upper half) are reproduced.
Code has been implemented that emits per-split counts and averages (#Bugs, #C/#M, #Comp, #Rep, #Reg, #Lines, #Funcs, #Files) for the full llvm-bench.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark statistics script and verify it produces per-split (easy/medium/hard/full) counts for #Bugs, #C, #M, #Comp, #Rep, #Reg, and Fixes averages (#Lines/#Funcs/#Files) as separate reported fields.

sub_tasks.requirements: The easy split of full llvm-bench contains 255 issues (176 crashes / 79 miscompilations), representing 76.3% of the dataset.

verification.spec: Filter llvm-bench to entries whose split label is 'easy' and count them. Assert count == 255 and that 176 have type crash, 79 have type miscompilation, and 255/334 rounded to a tenth is 76.3%.

sub_tasks.requirements: The medium split of full llvm-bench contains 44 issues (26 crashes / 18 miscompilations), representing 13.2% of the dataset.

verification.spec: Filter llvm-bench entries whose split label is 'medium' and count them. Assert count == 44 with 26 crashes / 18 miscompilations, and that 44/334 rounds to 13.2%.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hard split of full llvm-bench contains 35 issues (20 crashes / 15 miscompilations), representing 10.5% of the dataset.

verification.spec: Filter llvm-bench entries whose split label is 'hard' and count them. Assert count == 35 with 20 crashes / 15 miscompilations, and that 35/334 rounds to 10.5%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-split #Comp values for full llvm-bench are: easy=48, medium=18, hard=25.

verification.spec: Count number of distinct directly-affected middle-end components per split of full llvm-bench; verify easy=48, medium=18, hard=25.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-split #Rep values for full llvm-bench are: easy=1.4, medium=1.4, hard=1.7.

verification.spec: Compute average reproducers per issue for each split of full llvm-bench; verify easy=1.4, medium=1.4, hard=1.7.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-split #Reg values for full llvm-bench are: easy=734.1, medium=626.5, hard=756.6.

verification.spec: Compute average component-specific regression tests per issue for each split of full llvm-bench; verify easy=734.1, medium=626.5, hard=756.6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-split Fixes averages (#Lines / #Funcs / #Files) for full llvm-bench are: easy=9.1/1.0/1.0, medium=38.8/2.6/1.0, hard=47.6/4.9/2.7.

verification.spec: Compute per-split Fixes averages (lines/funcs/files) for full llvm-bench; verify easy=9.1/1.0/1.0, medium=38.8/2.6/1.0, hard=47.6/4.9/2.7.

sub_tasks.requirements: The llvm-bench live subset statistics (Table 1 lower half) are reproduced.
Code has been implemented that filters the full llvm-bench to produce llvm-bench live containing only issues from the most recent year (starting Aug 26, 2024).

verification.spec: Run the live subset construction script with a cutoff date Aug 26, 2024; verify the output includes only issues whose fixing-commit timestamp is on or after that date and excludes older issues from full llvm-bench.

sub_tasks.requirements: The llvm-bench live subset contains 229 issues total (160 crashes / 69 miscompilations).

verification.spec: Count issues in llvm-bench live; verify total=229 with 160 crashes and 69 miscompilations.

sub_tasks.requirements: llvm-bench live directly affects 43 middle-end components and indirectly affects 175 components.

verification.spec: Count number of directly-affected and indirectly-affected middle-end components across llvm-bench live; verify direct=43, indirect=175.

verification.spec: Compute #Rep and #Reg averages across all 229 llvm-bench live issues; verify #Rep=1.5 and #Reg=743.7.

sub_tasks.requirements: The affected-component distribution (Figure 2 and Appendix A.3) is reproduced.
Code has been implemented that computes the count of full-llvm-bench issues per directly-affected middle-end component and produces the Figure 2 breakdown.

verification.spec: Run the component-breakdown script over full llvm-bench and verify it emits a per-component issue count that reproduces the Figure 2 partitioning (top components broken out; remainder aggregated into 'Others').

sub_tasks.requirements: The top-affected components in Figure 2 match exactly: SLPVectorizer=79, LoopVectorize=79, InstCombine=54, ScalarEvolution=16, VectorCombine=13, ValueTracking=9, IR=7, ConstraintElimination=6, InstructionSimplify=5, SimplifyIndVar=4, and Others=78.

verification.spec: Count issues per component in full llvm-bench; verify SLPVectorizer=79, LoopVectorize=79, InstCombine=54, ScalarEvolution=16, VectorCombine=13, ValueTracking=9, IR=7, ConstraintElimination=6, InstructionSimplify=5, SimplifyIndVar=4, and remaining components summed as Others=78.

sub_tasks.requirements: The full Appendix A.3 component list is reproduced: 64 distinct components with their issue counts summing to 334 and matching the enumerated per-component counts (SLPVectorizer 79, LoopVectorize 79, InstCombine 54, ..., AggressiveInstCombine 1).

verification.spec: Verify Appendix A.3 lists exactly 64 distinct components, per-component counts summing to 334, and matching the enumerated pairs (SLPVectorizer 79, LoopVectorize 79, ..., AggressiveInstCombine 1).

sub_tasks.requirements: The 64 directly-affected components are drawn from the 184 middle-end components counted from LLVM 21.1.0's -O3 optimization pipeline.

verification.spec: Enumerate distinct passes in the LLVM 21.1.0 -O3 middle-end optimization pipeline; verify the total component count equals 184 and the 64 affected components are a subset of these.

sub_tasks.requirements: Regression-test coverage claims (shared vs component-specific tests) are reproduced.
Code has been implemented that, for each issue, enumerates both the component-specific regression tests and the shared regression tests inherited from other middle-end components.

verification.spec: For a sample issue, invoke the harness's test-enumeration function and verify it returns two distinct lists: component-specific regression tests (from the erroneous component) and shared regression tests (from other middle-end components).

sub_tasks.requirements: The average number of shared regression tests (from components other than the erroneous one) per issue exceeds 10,000 as reported in Section 2.2 / Appendix A.2.

verification.spec: Compute average shared regression tests (from components other than the erroneous one) per issue across full llvm-bench; verify value exceeds 10,000.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fraction of golden patches originally accepted by LLVM reviewers without further bug fixes is below 50% as reported in Appendix A.2.

verification.spec: For each golden fixing commit, inspect its GitHub PR review history; count the fraction merged without any post-review bug-fix commits and verify it is below 50%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the four-stage (Setup, Reason, Generate, Validate) llvm-autofix-mini agent with the specified ReAct loops, tool subset, breakpoint policy, and failure semantics.

Overall agent architecture and orchestration exist: llvm-autofix-mini is structured as a four-stage pipeline (Setup -> Reason -> Generate -> Validate), driven by a controller that gates transitions and enforces failure semantics.
Code has been implemented that defines an llvm-autofix-mini entry point which sequentially drives four named stages Setup, Reason, Generate, and Validate for a given llvm-bench issue.

verification.spec: Import the llvm-autofix-mini agent entry point and verify it exposes a driver function that invokes four named stages Setup, Reason, Generate, Validate in that order for a given issue.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that if the agent unexpectedly exits during Setup, Reason, or Generate (e.g., token/tool limit, context overflow, tool-call format violation), the run is recorded as a failure and no accepted patch is emitted.

verification.spec: Simulate token-limit, tool-limit, context-overflow, and malformed tool-call scenarios in Setup, Reason, and Generate stages; verify the agent records the run as a failure with the appropriate failure category and emits no accepted patch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that only a patch that reaches Stage IV Validate and passes offline validation is emitted as an accepted patch; any Stage IV validation failure yields a PostValError failure rather than an accepted patch.

verification.spec: Run Stage IV with a patch that fails offline validation and verify a PostValError failure is emitted (no accepted patch); then run with a patch that passes offline validation and verify an accepted patch is returned.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that restricts the agent's tool interface to exactly the enabled subset { find, grep, list, read, edit, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, preview, test } from llvm-autofix, and rejects any other tool invocation.

verification.spec: Inspect the llvm-autofix-mini agent's tool registry (e.g., import the agent module and enumerate its exposed tool names). Assert the set equals exactly {find, grep, list, read, edit, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, preview, test}. Then attempt to invoke a disallowed tool name (e.g., 'bash', 'shell', 'submit-patch') via the agent's dispatch entry point and assert it is rejected with a structured error rather than executed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the shared per-run limits used in the paper's evaluation: context window 64,000 tokens, chat limit 500 rounds, token limit 5,000,000 tokens, edit limit 25 calls, and online test limit 25 calls.

verification.spec: Load the agent's run-configuration (config file / defaults module) and assert: context_window==64000, chat_limit==500, token_limit==5_000_000, edit_limit==25, online_test_limit==25. Then simulate a run with a stubbed model that emits >25 edit calls and confirm the harness aborts with a ToolLimit failure at the 26th call.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that logs per-issue trajectories including stage transitions, tool calls with success/failure status, and final outcome (accepted patch or specific failure category), suitable for downstream failure-mode and tool-call analyses.

verification.spec: Run llvm-autofix-mini against a stubbed issue with a scripted model that triggers each stage transition and one failing tool call. Verify the output trajectory file contains (a) explicit Setup/Reason/Generate/Validate stage markers, (b) each tool call with tool name, arguments, and success/failure status, and (c) a final outcome field taking a value in {accepted, CtxtLimit, PostValError, RoundLimit, TokenLimit, ImplError, ProactiveExit, RuinLLVM, ToolLimit}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage I (Setup) configures the LLVM environment, launches the reproducer under gdb, pauses at a bug-type-specific breakpoint, and infers the erroneous component to seed later stages.
Code has been implemented in Stage I that invokes the llvm-autofix Reproduce & Cause tooling to validate that the issue's reproducer actually triggers the bug on the base commit before proceeding.

verification.spec: Instantiate Stage I on a mock issue whose reproducer does NOT trigger the bug at the base commit. Confirm Stage I calls the Reproduce & Cause tool (verify via a spy/mock on that tool) and, upon negative result, aborts the run before entering Stage II. Then repeat with a valid reproducer and confirm Stage I records a successful reproduction and proceeds.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented in Stage I that launches opt on the reproducer under gdb and leaves the process paused at a breakpoint ready for the Reason stage's debug/eval tool calls.

verification.spec: Run Stage I on a real llvm-bench issue (or a minimal LLVM build with a canned reproducer). After Setup completes, assert (a) a gdb subprocess is alive attached to opt, (b) opt is paused at a breakpoint (gdb 'info program' reports 'Program stopped'), and (c) a subsequent debug(cmd='frame 0') tool call returns non-empty frame info.

sub_tasks.requirements: For crash bugs, the Setup stage places the initial gdb breakpoint immediately before the crashing function identified from the stack trace of the direct-cause tool.

verification.spec: For a crash-type issue in llvm-bench with a known crashing function F from its stack trace, run Stage I and query gdb via the agent's debug tool to report the current breakpoint location. Assert the paused location is at (or immediately before) function F, matching the top-of-stack frame extracted by the direct-cause tool.

sub_tasks.requirements: For miscompilation bugs, the Setup stage places the initial gdb breakpoint before the first LLVM IR transformation applied by opt on the reproducer.

verification.spec: For a miscompilation-type issue, run Stage I and inspect the gdb state. Assert the breakpoint is placed at an entry point of the first IR-transformation pass in opt's pipeline for the reproducer (e.g., inside runOnFunction/run of the first pass), and that no IR transformation has yet been applied (IR module snapshot equals input reproducer).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that infers the erroneous LLVM middle-end component during Stage I and propagates it both into the Reason-stage prompt and into the component-specific online-test configuration used by test().

verification.spec: Run Stage I on an issue whose golden patch touches component C (e.g., SLPVectorizer). Assert (a) the inferred component recorded by Setup equals C or a superset containing C, (b) the Reason-stage system/user prompt string contains the component name, and (c) the online test() invocation in Stage III restricts regression tests to component C's directory.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that if Setup cannot reproduce the bug or cannot pause at the required breakpoint, Stage I aborts the run as a failure without entering the Reason stage.

verification.spec: Run Stage I with a mocked Reproduce & Cause tool that returns 'not reproducible'; assert the agent exits with a failure outcome and never enters Stage II (Reason). Repeat with a mock where gdb fails to hit the requested breakpoint; assert the same abort behavior. In both cases, verify no accepted patch is emitted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage II (Reason) runs a ReAct loop over debugging and knowledge tools to identify the bug's root cause, using only the read-only tool subset relevant to reasoning.
Code has been implemented that drives Stage II as a ReAct loop alternating Thought and Action steps, where each Action is a single tool call chosen from the Reason-stage tool subset.

verification.spec: Drive Stage II with a scripted model that emits three Thought/Action pairs. Assert that (a) each step's model output is parsed into a Thought string and exactly one Action (tool call), (b) the tool result is fed back as an Observation into the next prompt, and (c) any step lacking an Action or containing multiple Actions is rejected with a format error.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Reason stage exposes at least the tools debug(cmd), eval(expr), code(func), docs(func), langref(inst), find, grep, list, and read, with signatures matching those specified in Appendix B.1.

verification.spec: Enumerate the tools registered in the Reason stage of llvm-autofix-mini. Assert the set includes {debug, eval, code, docs, langref, find, grep, list, read}. For each tool, check the callable's signature (via inspect.signature) matches Appendix B.1: debug(cmd), eval(expr), code(func), docs(func), langref(inst), find(...), grep(...), list(...), read(...).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that debug and eval calls in the Reason stage operate on the live gdb session started in Stage I (e.g., 'frame 3', evaluating expressions like WidePhi) and return their output to the model.

verification.spec: With a live Stage I gdb session on a real reproducer, invoke debug(cmd='frame 3') via the Reason-stage tool dispatcher and assert the returned string matches gdb's own output for that command. Then invoke eval(expr='1+1') and assert output contains '2'; invoke eval on a known local variable at the current breakpoint and assert the output is non-empty and comes from the same gdb process (verify by PID).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that blocks any patch-modifying tool (edit, reset, preview, test) from being invoked during the Reason stage, so Stage II remains read-only with respect to the LLVM source tree.

verification.spec: During Stage II, attempt to invoke edit(...), reset(), preview(), and test() via the agent's tool dispatcher. Assert each call returns a structured error indicating the tool is not available in the current stage, and that the underlying LLVM source tree and build state are unchanged (compare git status / file hashes before and after).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Stage II terminates and transitions into Stage III when the agent emits a declared root-cause conclusion, which is then passed as context into the Generate-stage prompt.

verification.spec: Drive Stage II with a scripted model that, after two tool calls, emits a designated root-cause declaration (per the agent's schema, e.g., a 'root_cause' action or terminal message). Assert Stage II terminates and Stage III begins, and that the Stage III initial prompt contains the exact root-cause text emitted in Stage II.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Stage II respects the global token, round, and per-tool call budgets, aborting with the appropriate failure category (TokenLimit, RoundLimit, CtxtLimit) when any limit is reached.

verification.spec: Run Stage II with mock models that exceed each budget: (a) emit tokens until cumulative usage exceeds 5,000,000 tokens and assert failure outcome=='TokenLimit'; (b) emit >500 ReAct rounds and assert outcome=='RoundLimit'; (c) return a tool observation exceeding the 64K context window and assert outcome=='CtxtLimit'. In each case, verify no patch is emitted and the trajectory records the specific limit hit.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage III (Generate) runs a second ReAct loop that synthesizes and iteratively refines a patch using edit/reset/preview and online test() feedback until online tests pass.

Code has been implemented that starts Stage III as a fresh ReAct loop initialized with the root cause from Stage II and the inferred erroneous component, but without carrying over the full Reason-stage message history verbatim.

verification.spec: Log Stage II message history H2 and Stage III message history H3. Assert H3's initial system/user prompt contains (a) the declared root cause and (b) the inferred erroneous component, but does NOT contain the full H2 verbatim (e.g., prior Thought/Action/Observation triples are absent or summarized). Verify by substring checks on a sample of unique Stage II tool observations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Generate stage exposes the editing tools edit(file, text, replace), reset(), and preview() with the semantics described in Appendix B.1 (replace a text span, revert all changes, and show a unified-diff preview, respectively).

verification.spec: Verify tool signatures via inspect: edit(file, text, replace), reset(), preview(). Then in Stage III on a scratch checkout: (a) call edit(file=F, text=T, replace=R) and assert F's contents change so that R is replaced with T; (b) call preview() and assert output is a unified diff matching `git diff`; (c) call reset() and assert F reverts exactly to base-commit contents (hash matches).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Generate stage exposes an online test() tool that rebuilds LLVM, runs the reproducer(s) and the component-specific regression tests, and returns structured pass/fail feedback (including failing test names or diagnostics) to the agent.

verification.spec: In Stage III on a real llvm-bench issue: (a) apply the golden patch via edit(), call test(), and assert it triggers an LLVM rebuild (detect via build artifact timestamps) and returns a structured result with pass=True and lists the reproducer and component-specific regression tests actually executed; (b) apply an obviously broken patch, call test(), and assert the result contains pass=False with at least one failing test name or diagnostic.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the per-run edit limit of 25 edit() calls and online test limit of 25 test() calls in Stage III, producing a ToolLimit failure when either budget is exhausted.

verification.spec: Run Stage III with a scripted model that emits 26 edit() calls (no test()); assert the 26th call is refused and outcome=='ToolLimit'. Separately, emit 25 successful edits followed by 26 test() calls; assert the 26th test() is refused and outcome=='ToolLimit'. Verify counters are per-run and independent for edit vs test.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Stage III concludes successfully only when an invocation of test() reports that online testing (reproducer(s) plus component-specific regression tests) passes, at which point the current patch is forwarded to Stage IV.

verification.spec: Drive Stage III on a real issue: (a) with a scripted model applying the golden patch, verify that upon test() returning pass=True Stage III terminates and Stage IV receives the same patch (diff hash matches); (b) with a model whose test() calls only ever return pass=False, verify Stage III never transitions to Stage IV until either it exhausts a budget or an eventual pass=True.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that detects when the agent explicitly declares it cannot fix the issue and terminates Stage III as a ProactiveExit failure without emitting a patch.

verification.spec: Drive Stage III with a scripted model that emits the agent's designated 'give up' / cannot-fix declaration (per its action schema). Assert the run terminates immediately with outcome=='ProactiveExit', no test() has been invoked afterward, and no accepted patch is written to disk.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that if an edit corrupts the LLVM source tree to the point that rebuilds crash before regression tests can run, the run is classified as RuinLLVM in the failure taxonomy; the Generate stage additionally supports reset() to fully revert to the initial base-commit state on demand.

verification.spec: Simulate a Stage III edit that corrupts a critical LLVM header (e.g., inject a syntax error into llvm/include/llvm/IR/Instructions.h) then call test(). Assert the rebuild fails, the harness classifies the outcome as 'RuinLLVM' in the trajectory, and no accepted patch is emitted. Then, from that ruined state, call reset() and assert the working tree matches base-commit hashes exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that malformed tool calls in Stage III (arguments not matching the declared signatures) return a structured error to the model rather than crashing the harness, and repeated format violations accrue toward TokenLimit rather than silent success.

verification.spec: In Stage III, submit malformed tool calls (e.g., edit missing 'replace', test with unexpected kwargs, unknown tool name, malformed JSON). Assert (a) each returns a structured error observation to the model rather than raising an unhandled exception, (b) the harness process remains alive, and (c) the tokens spent on these erroneous exchanges count toward the token budget, eventually triggering TokenLimit if repeated indefinitely.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage IV (Validate) performs offline validation of the patch produced by Stage III, matching the post-generate validation used for both llvm-autofix-mini and the mini-SWE-agent baseline.

Code has been implemented that in Stage IV rebuilds LLVM with the Stage III patch applied and runs the full offline validation pipeline (reproducers plus the component's regression tests, with any additional cross-component or differential testing enabled by configuration).

verification.spec: Feed Stage IV a candidate patch on a real llvm-bench issue. Assert (a) LLVM is rebuilt at the base commit + patch (detect via build log / artifact timestamps), (b) the offline validation invokes the reproducer(s) via opt and the component's regression tests via llvm-lit, and (c) when a config flag enabling cross-component or differential testing is set, additional test suites (e.g., other components' lit tests, alive2 differential) are also executed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that emits the Stage III patch as an accepted patch if and only if Stage IV offline validation passes; otherwise the run is recorded as a PostValError failure with no accepted patch.

verification.spec: Run Stage IV with (a) the golden patch: assert it passes offline validation and the run writes an accepted-patch artifact whose diff equals the golden patch; (b) a patch that passes Stage III's component-specific tests but fails an offline cross-component test: assert no accepted-patch file is emitted and the trajectory records outcome=='PostValError'.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that Stage IV runs without any further LLM calls or tool invocations by the agent; the model has no opportunity to react to offline test results.

verification.spec: Inspect the llvm-autofix-mini Stage IV implementation: verify that after Stage III completes, the Validate stage executes offline tests as a deterministic script (rebuild + run tests) with no LLM API calls, no ReAct loop, and no tool-call handlers registered. Grep the source for any llm/model client invocation within the Stage IV code path and confirm none exist. Run a scripted end-to-end trial and confirm the trajectory log shows zero model messages after Stage III ends.

sub_tasks.requirements: Stage IV uses the same offline validation configuration (tests, tools, and pass/fail criteria) that the harness applies to mini-SWE-agent's submitted patches, so accepted-patch definitions are directly comparable between the two agents.

verification.spec: Compare the offline-validation code path invoked by llvm-autofix-mini Stage IV against the post-generate validation invoked for mini-SWE-agent submissions. Confirm both call the same underlying harness function/entrypoint with the same test set (reproducers + component regression tests + any permitted extended tests) and identical pass/fail criteria. Feed the same candidate patch to both agents' validation paths on one llvm-bench issue and assert identical accept/reject verdicts and identical test-list execution.

sub_tasks.requirements: Failure taxonomy and system prompts precisely match the paper's specification so downstream failure-mode analyses and cost accounting are reproducible.

Code has been implemented that classifies every non-accepted run into exactly one of the categories CtxtLimit, TokenLimit, RoundLimit, ToolLimit, ProactiveExit, RuinLLVM, PostValError, or ImplError, using the definitions described in Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Construct synthetic runs that trigger each failure mode (context overflow, token overflow, round overflow, tool-call overflow, agent-declared exit, corrupted LLVM tree, offline test failure, and internal harness exception) and confirm the classifier assigns each to exactly one of {CtxtLimit, TokenLimit, RoundLimit, ToolLimit, ProactiveExit, RuinLLVM, PostValError, ImplError}. Also verify that no run outputs multiple categories or an 'unknown' category.

sub_tasks.requirements: The llvm-autofix-mini system prompt used at evaluation time matches the one provided in Appendix E, including the four-stage description, the enumerated allowed tools, and the enforced limits.

verification.spec: Load the system prompt string used by llvm-autofix-mini at evaluation and diff it against the Appendix E text. Assert the prompt contains: the four stage names (Setup, Reason, Generate, Validate), the enumerated tool list (find, grep, list, read, edit, code, docs, langref, debug, eval, reset, preview, test), and the numerical limits (500 rounds, 5M tokens, 25 edits, 25 tests). Fail if any is missing or altered.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that internal harness exceptions unrelated to model behavior (i.e., bugs in llvm-autofix-mini itself) are surfaced as ImplError rather than being silently mapped to another failure category.

verification.spec: Inject a synthetic exception into an internal llvm-autofix-mini helper (e.g., raise RuntimeError in the debugger wrapper) and run the agent on a sample issue. Confirm the run is recorded with category ImplError, not TokenLimit/ProactiveExit/etc. Also confirm the stack trace or error message is preserved in the trajectory log for debugging.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral checks: the assembled llvm-autofix-mini agent behaves end-to-end as specified when driven by simple deterministic stubs or by the configured LLMs.

When driven by a scripted agent that only queries the debugger and then submits the exact golden patch for a sample llvm-bench crash issue, llvm-autofix-mini traverses Setup -> Reason -> Generate -> Validate and emits an accepted patch identical to the input.

verification.spec: Replace the LLM backend with a scripted stub that (a) in Stage II inspects one gdb frame then declares root cause, (b) in Stage III issues a single edit() applying the golden patch for a known llvm-bench crash issue then calls test(). Run the harness end-to-end on that issue. Assert the trajectory shows all four stages executed in order and the final accepted patch equals the golden patch byte-for-byte.

sub_tasks.requirements: When driven by a scripted agent that submits a syntactically valid but semantically wrong edit that fails only offline (Stage IV) tests, the harness records the run as PostValError and does not emit an accepted patch.

verification.spec: Use a scripted stub agent that in Stage III submits an edit which passes the online test() (e.g., disables the failing reproducer path narrowly) but fails a broader offline regression test in Stage IV. Confirm the harness records the run with failure category PostValError, produces no accepted patch, and reports the failing test name.

sub_tasks.requirements: When driven by a scripted agent that issues 25 edit() calls without ever calling test(), Stage III terminates with a ToolLimit failure attributed to the edit budget.

verification.spec: Use a scripted stub that in Stage III repeatedly calls edit() with trivial changes and never calls test(). After 25 edit() invocations, assert the harness terminates Stage III with failure category ToolLimit and the recorded reason attributes the limit to the edit budget (not the test budget or token budget).

sub_tasks.requirements: For a miscompilation issue, the initial gdb breakpoint set by Stage I halts execution strictly before opt applies its first IR transformation, verifiable by inspecting the paused program counter or backtrace against opt's transformation entry point.

verification.spec: Pick a miscompilation issue from llvm-bench. Run Stage I of llvm-autofix-mini and capture gdb state at the initial breakpoint. Confirm the current frame corresponds to a point before any IR transformation pass is executed (e.g., inside PassManager::run entry or before the first pass's runOnFunction/run), by comparing the backtrace against opt's known transformation entry point. Assert no transformation-side-effect functions appear below the current frame.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a crash issue, the initial gdb breakpoint set by Stage I halts execution strictly before entry into the function identified as the crashing frame by the Reproduce & Cause stack trace.

verification.spec: Pick a crash issue from llvm-bench. Extract the crashing frame from the Reproduce & Cause stack trace. Run Stage I and confirm gdb is paused at a breakpoint on entry to that function, before any statement in its body has executed (verify via `info frame` and `list` showing the function prologue).

sub_tasks.requirements: For any accepted-patch run of llvm-autofix-mini on llvm-bench live, the recorded trajectory contains at least one successful test() invocation in Stage III and no tool calls in Stage IV, matching the intended online/offline validation split.

verification.spec: For any accepted-patch trajectory produced by llvm-autofix-mini on llvm-bench live, parse the trajectory log and assert: (a) at least one test() call occurs during Stage III and its result is 'pass', (b) zero tool calls occur during Stage IV. Run this check across a sample of accepted-patch runs and require 100% conformance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integrate mini-SWE-agent with llvm-autofix tools as the canonical baseline agent, providing it the specified inputs (erroneous component, direct cause, post-generate validation) and system prompt from Appendix E.
Wire mini-SWE-agent into the llvm-autofix harness so it can be launched against llvm-bench issues as the canonical baseline agent.
Code has been implemented to install and invoke mini-SWE-agent (from the SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent repository) as an agent runner within the llvm-autofix benchmarking scripts.

verification.spec: Verify the llvm-autofix benchmarking scripts import or invoke mini-swe-agent from the SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent package (e.g., via pip-installed entrypoint or subprocess). Grep the repo for 'mini_swe_agent' or 'mini-swe-agent' references, confirm the package is listed in requirements/pyproject, and run a smoke test that launches mini-swe-agent on a trivial task and captures its output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that mini-SWE-agent runs inside an ubuntu:24.04 container/environment with all default bash tools (e.g., grep, sed, ls, cat) accessible to the agent.

verification.spec: Inspect the Dockerfile or container spec used for mini-SWE-agent runs and assert the base image is ubuntu:24.04. Launch the container and confirm `grep`, `sed`, `ls`, `cat`, `find`, `awk` are all resolvable via `which` and executable.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to expose llvm-autofix command-line tools (at least opt, llvm-lit, and the harness `test` command) on the PATH inside the mini-SWE-agent execution environment.

verification.spec: Launch the mini-SWE-agent execution environment and run `which opt`, `which llvm-lit`, `which test` (or the harness's exposed test command). Assert all three resolve to executable files. Additionally run `opt --version` and confirm it reports an LLVM version consistent with the benchmark's base commits.

sub_tasks.requirements: Provide mini-SWE-agent with the three extra inputs specified in Section 3: inferred erroneous component, direct cause, and post-generate validation.
Code has been implemented to compute the inferred erroneous LLVM middle-end component for each llvm-bench issue and pass it into mini-SWE-agent's initial prompt.

verification.spec: Take a sample llvm-bench issue with a known erroneous component (e.g., SLPVectorizer). Invoke the llvm-autofix component-inference tool and confirm it outputs the expected component. Then launch mini-SWE-agent for that issue and inspect the initial prompt sent to the model; assert the prompt contains the inferred component name as a discrete field.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that, for crash bugs, the direct cause supplied to mini-SWE-agent includes the stack trace produced by opt with non-interesting frames eliminated (matching the Reproduce & Cause tool output).

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)
A CLI or script exists that iterates over all issues in llvm-bench (or llvm-bench live) and dispatches an agent (llvm-autofix-mini or mini-SWE-agent) per issue.

verification.spec: Invoke the benchmark runner in dry-run mode over a small subset (e.g., 3 issues) of llvm-bench; assert the runner enumerates each issue exactly once, dispatches the configured agent per issue, and returns a per-issue result record.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each processed issue, the harness emits the validated patch (or a structured error for failed runs) as a machine-readable artifact.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark runner over a small subset with a mock agent that returns a fixed patch for one issue and errors for another; assert output directory contains a per-issue file with either a valid unified diff (patch) or a structured error record (JSON with error type).

sub_tasks.requirements: For each processed issue, the harness records per-issue cost (token counts and/or dollar cost) and trajectory (sequence of tool calls) in a log file.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark runner with a mock agent that emits recorded tool calls and token usage; assert the produced log includes a per-issue entry containing (a) token counts, (b) monetary cost, and (c) an ordered list of tool calls with arguments.

sub_tasks.requirements: When the golden patch is accessible, the harness builds a second opt binary from the golden-patched LLVM source for differential testing.

verification.spec: Invoke the harness's differential-testing setup on a small llvm-bench issue whose golden patch is available; assert two opt binaries are produced (one from the agent's patch, one from the golden patch) at distinct paths and both are executable.

sub_tasks.requirements: The harness runs both the agent-patched opt and the golden-patched opt on the same reproducer set and collects their outputs.

verification.spec: For a chosen issue, invoke the differential test harness; assert both opt binaries are executed on the identical reproducer(s) with identical command-line flags, and that both stdout/stderr/exit-code outputs are captured for each.

sub_tasks.requirements: The harness diffs the post-optimization IR from agent-patched vs golden-patched opt and reports semantic mismatches (e.g., via alive2 or IR diff) as part of validation feedback.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic 'agent patch' that produces different post-optimization IR than the golden patch on a test reproducer; run the differential validation; assert the harness flags a semantic mismatch and returns a structured report identifying the differing reproducer.
